revolution.title: Huang Chao’s revolt shakes the Tang
revolution.line: After drought, famine and higher taxes, failed exam candidate Huang Chao led a revolt that took Chang’an; the Tang never recovered.

revolution.title: The Red Turbans rise against the Yuan
revolution.line: After Yellow River floods and famine, drafted dike workers joined the Red Turbans against Mongol rule, which collapsed in 1368.

revolution.title: The Ciompi revolt seizes Florence
revolution.line: Florence’s wool workers, barred from the guilds that ran the city and crushed by taxes, seized the government for six weeks.

carrington.title: Tree rings record the 774 solar storm
carrington.line: Tree rings worldwide record a carbon-14 spike, likely from a solar storm, the strongest in 11,000 years; a repeat could cripple satellites.

carrington.title: The great aurora over Japan and China
carrington.line: Auroras lit skies over Japan and China for about nine nights, and Cook’s crew saw them near Timor, a storm rivaling Carrington’s.

scramble.title: Castile and Portugal split Africa’s Atlantic coast
scramble.line: After a naval war over Guinea’s gold and slaves, Castile got the Canaries and Portugal sole rights to Africa’s coast beyond them.

scramble.title: The Treaty of Tordesillas
scramble.line: Spain and Portugal split the world along a line west of Cape Verde, leaving Africa’s coasts to Portugal; other powers rejected it.

ellis.title: Ur builds a wall against the Amorites
ellis.line: As Amorite herders moved into Sumer, Ur’s king built a wall called “Holding back the Tidnum”; Amorite dynasties later ruled Mesopotamia anyway.

ellis.title: London rebels massacre Flemish immigrants
ellis.line: After Edward III welcomed Flemish weavers, rebels in the Peasants’ Revolt hunted Flemings in London, killing dozens identified by their accents.

sykes.title: Rome splits Macedonia into four republics
sykes.line: Rome cut Macedonia into four republics, banning marriage across the new lines; in 149 BC the pretender Andriscus reunited it in revolt.

tariffs.title: Rhodes goes to war over Byzantium’s toll
tariffs.line: Byzantium taxed ships leaving the Black Sea; Rhodes, speaking for the merchants, declared war and forced the toll’s repeal.

tariffs.title: The Hanseatic League embargoes Flanders
tariffs.line: When Flanders raised taxes on Hanseatic traders, the League embargoed it and nearly caused a famine until the count expanded their privileges.

tariffs.title: The Tariff of Abominations
tariffs.line: Congress sharply raised import duties; Southern planters, fearing lost cotton sales to Britain, protested, and South Carolina later tried to nullify it.

martians.title: A false Nero appears in Greece
martians.line: According to Tacitus, a lyre-playing lookalike claiming to be the dead emperor Nero gathered deserters in Greece until Roman soldiers killed him.

martians.title: The letter of Prester John
martians.line: A forged letter from a mythical Christian king in Asia, “Prester John,” swept Europe; a pope wrote to him in 1177.

martians.title: Valla exposes the Donation of Constantine
martians.line: Lorenzo Valla proved the Donation of Constantine, a decree popes had cited for centuries to back their worldly power, was a forgery.

martians.title: The Great Moon Hoax
martians.line: The New York Sun reported that astronomer John Herschel had found bat-winged people on the Moon; the hoax went unexposed for weeks.

suez.title: Vasco da Gama sails around Africa
suez.line: To bypass Venice and Egypt’s hold on the Red Sea spice route, Portugal’s Vasco da Gama sailed around Africa and reached India.

tiananmen.title: Han China purges its student critics
tiananmen.line: When Imperial Academy students backed officials denouncing palace eunuchs, Emperor Huan arrested some 200 and banned the critics from office for life.

tiananmen.title: Song students besiege the palace gate
tiananmen.line: Imperial University students led crowds to Kaifeng’s palace gate demanding a sacked minister back; the court yielded, but later executed their leader.

y2k.title: A glitch crashes the ARPANET
y2k.line: A hardware fault sent corrupted routing updates circling endlessly, and for several hours almost no ARPANET node could reach another.
